title: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition - Finance & Legal Guidance 2027
author: Claire Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s operating guidance for budgeting & forecasting cadence, contracts & legal review process, procurement approval workflows, and revenue recognition & billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business leaders responsible for planning, approving, and recording company financial commitments.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood business units globally. Exceptions (e.g., customer-specific legal requirements, regulated deployments) must be routed through Legal and Finance for case-by-case handling.

Key owners
- Finance: Claire Thompson (Director, FP&A) — budgeting & forecasting cadence, revenue recognition guidance, financial reporting
- Legal: Jordan Kim (Counsel) — contract reviews, clause standardization, exceptions
- Procurement: Marcus Li (Head of Procurement) — vendor onboarding, purchase orders, vendor agreements
- Revenue Operations: Sofia Ruiz — billing schedules, invoicing, collections

1) Budgeting & Forecasting

Objective: Produce reliable 12-month rolling forecasts and an annual budget that balance growth plans with predictable cash management and capacity investments.

Cadence and deliverables
- Annual budget cycle: kickoff in October; departmental submissions due by November 30; Finance consolidation and executive review in December; Board-approved budget by January 31.
- Quarterly reforecast: End-of-quarter reforecast due within 2 weeks of quarter close (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4).
- Monthly rolling forecast: Updated by finance and shared with GTM and Engineering on the 7th business day of each month.

Inputs required from teams
- Headcount plan with monthly hire/start dates and grade-level compensation
- Operating expense line items (SaaS, cloud, third-party services) with current commitments and renewal dates
- Product & infra capacity plans (Dedicated/Private expansion, on-prem packaging costs)
- Sales pipeline by close probability and expected billing start date

Forecasting controls and assumptions
- Revenue: use weighted pipeline by probability buckets (>=90%, 60–89%, 30–59%, <30%) with historical conversion factors applied by sales segment
- Cloud & GPU costs: normalize current run rates and apply planned capacity adjustments; include a 5% contingency for unexpected spot pricing changes unless otherwise approved
- Hiring ramp: new hires included at 75% of fully-loaded cost in the hiring quarter as default ramp assumption

Deliverables and templates
- Monthly: Rolling forecast workbook (Finance template) — submit to /drive/finance/rolling-forecast-templates
- Annual: Budget workbook (with capex schedules for Dedicated/Private deployments)

2) Contracts & Legal Process (Standard vendor and customer agreements)

Principles
- Use standardized templates maintained by Legal whenever possible. Avoid unilateral edits to critical clauses (IP, data protection, indemnity, liability caps, termination for convenience).
- All legally binding contracts require a Contract Review and an authorized signatory.

Contract review workflow (standard flow)
1. Request: Owner (Sales/Product/Procurement) creates a Contract Intake ticket in the Legal queue with draft contract and redlines (if any). Include business rationale, estimated ARR or contract value, and expected execution date.
2. Triage: Legal acknowledges within 2 business days. If high-risk clauses present (data residency, regulated customer, export controls), Legal flags and schedules an expedited review.
3. Risk assessment: Legal assesses regulatory, IP, indemnity, and liability issues and documents required mitigations. Finance reviews for revenue accounting implications and pricing terms.
4. Negotiation: Legal leads negotiation with counterparties; Procurement supports vendor commercial negotiations for supplier agreements.
5. Approval: For contract values exceeding approval thresholds (see Procurement thresholds below) obtain sign-off from Finance (for revenue/discount) and Legal (for terms).
6. Execution: Authorized signatory executes and Procurement/Contract Admin uploads fully-signed agreement to the contract repository (/drive/contracts) and registers key metadata (counterparty, effective date, renewal date, contract value, owner, confidentiality level).

Minimum documentation required for customer contracts
- Fully-executed agreement PDF
- Approved SOW or order form with pricing and term
- Revenue recognition assessment (Finance) indicating timing and pattern of revenue recognition (e.g., over time vs. point in time)

Common legal guardrails
- Standard liability cap: liability limited to the greater of $1,000,000 or 12 months of fees, unless approved by Legal + CFO.
- Data protection: require SOC 2 or equivalent for vendors processing customer data; customer-facing agreements must include standard data processing addendum (DPA).
- Export controls: for deployments in restricted jurisdictions, Legal must review for export-control implications.

3) Procurement Procedures and Approval Thresholds

Purpose: Ensure consistent vendor selection, cost control, and contractual oversight. Procurement manages vendor onboarding, purchase orders (POs), vendor master data, and PO approvals.

Procurement approval matrix (effective 2027-02-01)
- <$5,000: Manager approval (email justification)
- $5,000–$49,999: Director approval + Procurement notification
- $50,000–$249,999: VP approval + Procurement & Finance review
- $250,000–$999,999: CFO approval + Legal review + Procurement
- >= $1,000,000: Executive Committee approval (CFO, CEO, Head of Product) + Legal & Procurement (requires Board notification if multi-year commitment impacts cash or off-balance obligations)

Procurement process (steps)
1. Requisition: Requesting owner submits Procurement Requisition form with justification, budget code, and estimated value.
2. Sourcing: Procurement runs competitive sourcing (when applicable), collects quotes, and performs vendor risk checks (security posture, financial stability).
3. Approval: Obtain approvals per matrix. Attach signed vendor master data and required compliance evidence (SOC2, ISO, insurance certificates).
4. PO issuance: Procurement issues PO referencing the negotiated contract. POs are required for all vendor payments unless invoice cites a fully-executed supplier agreement and Procurement has waived PO requirement in writing.
5. Receipt & payment: Business owner confirms goods/services received; AP processes payment per payment terms.

Vendor onboarding checklist
- Completed W9/W-8 or local tax forms
- Bank/payment details verified via Procurement team (no vendor changes without dual verification)
- Insurance certificate on file (commercial general liability / cyber liability thresholds per vendor type)
- Security questionnaire or SOC 2 report for vendors handling sensitive/customer data

Emergency procurement (accelerated process)
- Use only for critical outages or time-sensitive procurements. Must be documented and retroactively approved by Procurement and Finance within 5 business days.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Objective: Ensure revenue is recognized in accordance with applicable accounting standards (ASC 606 / IFRS 15) and reflected accurately in monthly close and customer billing. This section provides high-level guidance; material or unusual transactions must be escalated to Revenue Ops and Finance for formal accounting assessment.

Revenue recognition principles
- Identify contract(s) with customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, and recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- Typical Redwood revenue streams: Hosted API usage (usage-based), Dedicated reserved capacity (subscription/commit), Private deployments (license + services), Professional services, and Marketplace/third-party add-ons.

Common patterns and examples
- Usage-based Hosted API: Recognize revenue as tokens are delivered (over time). Invoice monthly in arrears based on measured usage.
- Dedicated reserved capacity (subscription): Recognize ratably over the contractual period unless evidence indicates distinct performance obligations (e.g., dedicated migration services) that should be recognized separately.
- One-time professional services (e.g., on-prem install, migration): Recognize on completion of the service if criteria for satisfaction at a point in time are met, or over time if customer controls the asset as it is created.
- Variable consideration (discounts, credits, rebates): Estimate using most likely amount or expected value method and constrain if probable to result in significant reversal. Practical expedient to exclude insignificant financing components if original expected duration < 12 months.

Billing & invoicing practices
- Standard billing cadence: Monthly invoices unless contract specifies otherwise. Invoice generation typically within 5 business days after month-end for usage-based billing.
- Net terms: Standard is Net 30 for established customers; extended terms require Finance approval and a signed credit arrangement.
- Early termination and refunds: Contract must define termination charges and refund policy. Finance calculates and approves any refund or credit memo; Revenue Ops records corresponding adjustments to deferred revenue.

Cutoff and month-end close responsibilities
- Sales/Customer Success: provide final signed orders and effective dates to Revenue Ops by close cutoff (2 business days before month end) to ensure correct booking.
- Revenue Ops: maintain deferred revenue schedules and recognize revenue per the recognized pattern; prepare monthly revenue substantiation working papers.
- Finance (FP&A): incorporate recognized revenue into monthly reporting and variance analysis against forecast.

Internal controls and audit readiness
- All contracts and POs must be retained in the contract repository with searchable metadata.
- Segregation of duties: Sales/Account Execs cannot post customer invoices; Billing and AR are handled by Revenue Ops and AP respectively.
- Periodic audits: Finance will run an annual revenue recognition audit and quarterly spot checks on high-value contracts (> $250k).

5) Exceptions, Escalations, and Amendments

- Contract exceptions (changes to liability, IP, data residency, or material payment terms) require Legal and Finance sign-off and must be documented with rationale and approvers.
- Procurement exceptions (single-source, non-competed purchases) require a documented waiver from the Head of Procurement and CFO.
- Revenue accounting judgments (e.g., principal vs. agent, contract modifications) must be escalated to Revenue Ops and documented in the contract file.

Appendices
A. Procurement forms & templates
- Procurement Requisition template (link: /drive/procurement/templates/requisition.xlsx)
- Vendor onboarding checklist (link: /drive/procurement/vendor-onboarding-checklist.pdf)

B. Contract clause library (maintained by Legal)
- Standard terms index: limitation of liability, indemnity, DPA, export control clause, audit rights, termination for convenience

C. Example journal treatment (summary)
- Hosted usage invoice (monthly in arrears): DR Accounts Receivable; CR Deferred Revenue (if invoice issued in advance) / CR Revenue (when recognized)
- Subscription (annual prepaid): DR Cash; CR Deferred Revenue. Recognize monthly: DR Deferred Revenue; CR Revenue.

Document governance
- Owner: Finance (Claire Thompson). Legal & Procurement co-maintainers.
- Review cadence: Annual policy review in Q4, or ad-hoc as required by regulatory or business changes.
- Change log: maintain a short change log in the contract repository entry and notify teams via Finance newsletter when material changes occur.

Contact points
- Finance (FP&A & Revenue Ops): finance@redwood-inference.internal
- Legal: legal@redwood-inference.internal
- Procurement: procurement@redwood-inference.internal

If you have questions about application of this guidance to a specific transaction, please create a Legal intake ticket and copy Finance for a coordinated review.
